previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Addison’s disease, hypothyroidism, and migraines was admitted for headache, neck pain, nausea, and vomiting, concerning for an adrenal crisis. She had recently increased her prednisone dose to 7.5 mg to prevent hospitalization. Evaluation showed stable vital signs, normal electrolytes, and no evidence of adrenal insufficiency. Symptoms were attributed to a viral illness and muscle spasm likely triggered by poor sleep and prior neck injury from a car accident. She received IV fluids, stress-dose hydrocortisone, and pain management. Her nausea resolved, and neck pain improved with medication. Liver enzymes were mildly elevated but trending downward, likely due to prior acetaminophen use. She was given pneumococcal vaccine and started on Bactrim for PCP prophylaxis due to chronic steroid use. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue her baseline prednisone, use sumatriptan for migraines, and follow up with her endocrinologist.

History of Present Illness:
Mrs. ___ is a ___ ___ woman with a past medical history 
of Addison's disease and hypothyroidism (diagnosed ___ years ago) 
presenting after two days of diarrheal illness, with weakness 
and lightheadedness yesterday.  

 
Mrs. ___ had few medical problems and three unremarkable 
births prior to falling into a ___ state with adrenal 
failure. Her skin was dark and she felt as if everything were 
surreal. She was treated at ___ and recovered well. 
Hypothyroidism was also found at the same time.  

 
Since that time she gradually learnt the signs of corticosteroid 
excess, need for extra cover and the ways in which she needs to 
treat herself with more care. Her endocrinologist has warned her 
against easily starting high stress dose steroids and she now 
tried to rest and relax when unwell. This is why she will come 
to the hospital when feeling unwell with a somewhat lower 
threshold.  

 
Two days ago she experienced the acute onset of diarrhea and 
bloating. She had about five bowel movements that night, which 
were fatty, watery and foul smelling. There was no blood. She 
does not know of any infectious contacts, but things in her 
home, where she lives with her husband, are presently in 
dissarray given ongoing renovations. There are not presently 
kitchen facilities and food preparation occurs on a small table. 
 

 
She slept poorly but was not incontinent of stool. The next 
morning she vomited mucus like clear fluid, without bile. Later 
that next day she felt very weak and lightheaded, despite trying 
to stay on top of fluid intake, drinking half a gallon of fluids 
and taking bullion to supplement sodium (given Addison's). She 
also endorses some vertigo (sense of room spinning).  

 
Yesterday, she spoke to her Endocrinologist, Dr ___. Spoke 
with the patient by telephone with lab results, advising her to 
take an extra tablet on Florinef given higher K, along with 
extra ___ liquids. Resuming usual Florinef dose 
today. Instructed to call later this week if having recurrent

Brief Hospital Course:
Precis
  This is a pleasant and insightful patient with Addison's 
disease and recent diarrhea with likely volume depletion and 
adrenal insufficiency resulting in lightheadedness. Her 
laboratory data may be suggestive of mild hypocortisolism with 
borderline hyponatremia and hyperkalemia, rather than 
hypernatremia and hypokalemia as might be expected with 
diarrheal illness. She appears somewhat anxious about adrenal 
insufficiency and was keen to be monitored in the hospital. She 
stayed overnight receiving four liters of normal saline, 
correcting these electrolyte disturbances, and repletion of 
magnesium. 
 
Hospital Course by Problem  

Diarrhea  
  Has now passed. Duration, symptoms, signs consistent with 
viral diarrheal illness, perhaps Noravirus. She has now 
improved, but is likely still contagious given resolution less 
than 72 hours ago. Given that this is ___, other causes 
seem unlikely (such as inflammation, protazoal, endocrine). 
Bacterial diarrhea is also possible. Supportive hydration and 
monitoring of electrolytes. Labs will be ___ on ___ 
and sent to her PCP and ___.  

Addison's Disease  
  Possibilty under slightly less control at present given 
electrolytes and symptoms, likely because of intercurrent 
illness. She is closely followed by Dr. ___ will also be 
following her labs on ___ and subsequently. Double dose of 
prednisone for two days and double dose of fludrocort for one 
day was recommended. She was orthostatic (appropriate 
tachycardia with 4 mmHg fall in systolic pressure after 
standing, suggestive of low peripheral vascular 
resistance/hypovolemia). She received 4L of normal saline. 
 
Hypothyroidism  
  No tremor and relexes within normal limits suggesting that 
thyroid therapy is appropriate. TSH normal at 3.1. Continued 
synthroid at 88 mcg QD.
 
Hypotension and Tachycardia
  She reports that these are typical with systolic pressures 
previously 140 then in 110s after Addison's diagnosis. Heart 
rate is typically around 100 and may be higher with 
exercise/illness. We did not continue her beta blocker with 
concern for orthostatic hypotension with rate compensation. In 
addition, we felt that her sinus tachycardia was physiologic. In 
addition, recent outpatient notes do not show metoprolol on her 
medication list. 

Back Pain  
  Rhomboid busitis. Will continue treatment with analgesics. 
Patient requested IV dilaudid, but convinced her to trial oral 
opioids. Unfortunately given IV Dilaudid in ED, which was likely 
excessive. Oxycodone 5 mg BID PRN on ward as previous prescribed 
- this was not refilled on discharge.

Depression/Anxiety/Insomnia  
  Patient appears euthymic, but was slightly anxious, 
understandably but perhaps excessively, about Addisonian crisis. 
Continued clonazepam PRN. 

Migraine  
  Inactive during her stay. Sumitriptan is taken for migraine 
but was not required. 

Low bone mineral density  
  Continued vitamin D and Ca. She takes Fosamax 70 mg once per 
week.  

GERD  
  Given pantoprazole in hospital and then returned to home 
Nexium on discharge.  

Diet 
  Without sodium restricition given Addison's and hyponatremia.

Prophylaxis  
  Subcutaneous heparin, PPI.
